messages:
alex: Quick UX spike — I tried swapping a few labels in the playground schema editor to see if it helps discoverability for tool-calling. Figma link: https://figma.com/s/xyz (private).

maria: Nice. Which labels did you change?

alex: Short list: 'Invoke' -> 'Run', 'Tool output' -> 'Result', 'Function defs' -> 'Tool config'. Rationale: less jargon for product folks.

sam: I'm generally for simpler verbs. One accessibility snag: screen readers currently read the small 'invoke' icon as 'button' only. We need meaningful aria-labels.

joni: Agreed. Proposal: add aria-labels that include the tool name and action. Example snippet:```<li role="listitem" aria-label="Run tool: translate_text">...``` Also ensure focus outline for keyboard users on the tool chip.

maria: Should the run history group entries by invocation or by model message? Right now a single user prompt with 3 tool calls shows as 4 flat items, which feels noisy.

alex: I mocked a grouped view — collapsible invocation frames with a summary row. Summary shows number of tool calls + elapsed time, expand to see each call with its result. Keeps timeline compact.

sam: Love the grouping. For copy: 'expand' vs 'show details' — which reads better in small screens? 'Show details' is clearer imo.

joni: Another a11y nit: the collapse chevron needs 24px hit target. Right now it's 16px and fails keyboard muscle memory tests. Also need a visible focus state beyond default OS outline.

alex: Noted. I'll bump hit target and add focus ring token.

maria: Small copy tweak: change 'Tool result' header to 'Tool result (structured)' when a schema is attached, so users know there's a parseable output.

sam: Good call. Also consider adding a tiny inline badge: 'schema' that opens a quick preview on hover/focus — keyboard accessible.

deploy-bot: Deployed playground/ux/label-spike to staging at 1976543300.

alex: Thanks — can everyone spot-check staging? Focus on screenreader flow and run history density.

maria: I'll run a quick NVDA pass and list findings here by EOD.

joni: I'll validate keyboard-only nav and tab order.

sam: I'll test on mobile viewport and share any copy collisions.

alex: Great. If we get no blockers, I'll land the accessibility fixes + grouping on a small flags rollout. :thumbsup:
